subskill: Time saved when a rate increases by a percent
grade_rationale: High for grade 7 (7.RP.A.3): a 60% faster rate does not cut the time by 60%. The student finds the new rate, both times, and subtracts. Grade-7 students commonly cut the old time by 60%, add 60 pages per minute instead of 60%, or stop at the new rate.
prompt: An old printer prints 50 pages per minute. A new printer prints 60% faster than the old printer. How many fewer minutes does the new printer take than the old printer to print 11,000 pages?
explanation: The old printer takes 11,000 / 50 = 220 minutes. The new printer prints 60% faster: 50 x 1.6 = 80 pages per minute, so it takes 11,000 / 80 = 137.5 minutes. It takes 220 - 137.5 = 82.5 fewer minutes.
quantity_asked: how many fewer minutes the new printer takes

plugback.why: A time saved cannot be checked without both times, which is the task.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. The new rate is below the key; the 60%-cut time and the add-60-pages saving are above.
intermediate_check: 80 is an option: it is the solved new rate, offered as the wrong-variable error and named in distractor_meta. 220 and 137.5 are not options (137.5 would be key / 0.6, a printed-multiplier pair, so it was left out).
cheap_bound_check: Printed-multiplier bracket: 1.6 lies between 1.5 and 2, so the new time is between 1/2 and 2/3 of 220 and the saving is between 73.3 and 110; this strikes 120 only (80, 82.5 and 88 lie inside). The looser "less than twice as fast" bound (saving under 110) strikes the same 120. One option struck.
shape_check: Options are whole numbers and one one-decimal number (82.5).

subskill: Change in the output of a linear formula when the input changes
grade_rationale: Mid for grade 6 (6.EE.A.2c): the student evaluates a real-world formula at two inputs (or sees that the +32 drops out) and subtracts. Grade-6 students commonly add 32 to the Celsius change as if F were C + 32, combine the two temperatures by adding instead of subtracting, or report one Fahrenheit temperature instead of the change.
prompt: The formula F = (9/5)C + 32 changes a temperature of C degrees Celsius to F degrees Fahrenheit. A pot of water was heated from 1 degree Celsius to 50 degrees Celsius. By how many degrees Fahrenheit did the temperature of the water rise?
explanation: At 1 degree Celsius, F = (9/5)(1) + 32 = 1.8 + 32 = 33.8. At 50 degrees Celsius, F = (9/5)(50) + 32 = 90 + 32 = 122. The rise is 122 - 33.8 = 88.2 degrees Fahrenheit. (The +32 is in both temperatures, so the rise is (9/5)(50 - 1) = (9/5)(49) = 88.2.)
quantity_asked: the rise in temperature in degrees Fahrenheit

plugback.why: A rise in Fahrenheit cannot be checked without converting both temperatures, which is the task.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. The rise-plus-32 error is below the key; the added-temperatures error and the final Fahrenheit temperature are above.
intermediate_check: 122 is an option: it is the solved Fahrenheit temperature at 50 C, offered as the wrong-variable error and named in distractor_meta. 33.8 and the Celsius rise 49 are not options (49 is never an option: key / 49 is the printed 9/5).
cheap_bound_check: Printed-multiplier bracket: the Fahrenheit rise is 9/5 times the Celsius rise 49, so it lies strictly between 49 and 98; this strikes 122 only (81, 88.2, 91.8 lie inside). Multiple-of: a whole-number Celsius rise times 9/5 is a multiple of 1.8; 81 = 1.8 x 45, 88.2 = 1.8 x 49 and 91.8 = 1.8 x 51 all pass, so this strikes only 122, the same option. One option struck in all.
shape_check: Options are whole numbers and one-decimal numbers (81 and 122 whole, 88.2 and 91.8 one decimal); the key shares its form with a distractor.
interior_parity_check: Middle values 88.2 and 91.8; both one-decimal multiples of 1.8, neither cleaner.
arith_class_check: Every option but 122 is a multiple of 1.8 (the class the 9/5 factor forces); 122 is already struck by the bracket.

subskill: When one linear amount is twice another
grade_rationale: High for grade 8 (8.EE.C.7b): the student writes 760 + 6w = 2(240 + 7w), distributes the 2 to both terms, and solves. Grade-8 students commonly double only the starting amount or only the weekly amount, ignore Ana's deposits, or add the rates.
prompt: Ana has $760 in a savings account and adds $6 to it each week. Ben has $240 in his account and adds $7 to it each week. Neither of them takes any money out. After how many weeks will Ana have exactly twice as much money in her account as Ben has in his?
explanation: After w weeks Ana has 760 + 6w and Ben has 240 + 7w. Set 760 + 6w = 2(240 + 7w) = 480 + 14w. Then 280 = 8w, so w = 35. Check: Ana has 760 + 210 = 970 and Ben has 240 + 245 = 485, and 970 = 2 x 485.
quantity_asked: the number of weeks until Ana has twice as much as Ben

plugback.why: An option can be checked by computing both balances after that many weeks; the key is reached at try 3 ascending.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. Errors fall on both sides: adding the rates and ignoring Ana's deposits are below the key; the half-doubled equation is above.
intermediate_check: Solved intermediates are 280, 8, 970 and 485; none is an option.
cheap_bound_check: No sign, size or parity fact read off the stem strikes two options; all are whole numbers of weeks.

subskill: Average rate of change of a nonlinear function over an interval
grade_rationale: Mid for grade 8 (8.F.B.4 with 8.F.A.3): A = s^2 is not linear, so the student finds the change in area and divides by the change in side. Grade-8 students commonly divide by one of the side lengths instead of the change in side, or add the two areas instead of subtracting.
prompt: The area A, in square centimeters, of a square with sides s centimeters long is A = s^2. As the side length grows from 14 centimeters to 49 centimeters, by how many square centimeters does the area grow, on average, for each 1-centimeter increase in side length?
explanation: At s = 14 the area is 196 square centimeters, and at s = 49 it is 2,401 square centimeters. The area grows by 2,401 - 196 = 2,205 square centimeters while the side grows by 49 - 14 = 35 centimeters, so on average it grows 2,205 / 35 = 63 square centimeters per centimeter.
quantity_asked: the average growth in area per 1-centimeter increase in side

plugback.why: An average rate cannot be checked without both areas, which is the task.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. Dividing by the final side is below the key; adding the areas and dividing by the starting side are above.
intermediate_check: Solved intermediates 196, 2,401, 2,205 and 35 are not options.
cheap_bound_check: Increment bound: each 1-cm step from s to s + 1 adds 2s + 1, from 29 (at 14) to 97 (at 48), so the average lies strictly between 29 and 97; this strikes 157.5 only. Magnitude: no option approaches the total change 2,205. One option struck.
shape_check: Options are whole numbers and one-decimal numbers.

subskill: Original amount of a mixture from its percent before and after adding one part
grade_rationale: High for grade 7 (7.RP.A.3 with 7.EE.B.4a): adding juice changes both the amount of juice and the total. The student sets up 0.15N + 24 = 0.25(N + 24) and solves. Grade-7 students commonly treat the added 24 liters as a percent of the drink by itself (25%, 15% or the 10-point rise).
prompt: A tank holds a drink made only of juice and water, and 15% of the drink is juice. Ella adds 24 liters of juice and nothing else. Now 25% of the drink in the tank is juice. How many liters of drink were in the tank before Ella added the juice?
explanation: Let N be the liters of drink before. The juice was 0.15N. After adding 24 liters of juice there are 0.15N + 24 liters of juice in N + 24 liters of drink, and this is 25%: 0.15N + 24 = 0.25(N + 24) = 0.25N + 6. So 0.10N = 18 and N = 180. Check: 27 + 24 = 51 liters of juice in 204 liters, and 51 / 204 = 25%.
quantity_asked: the number of liters in the tank before the juice was added

plugback.why: An option can be checked by finding 15% of it, adding 24 liters of juice, and testing for 25%; the key is reached at try 3 ascending.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. The two percent-of-24 errors are below the key; the 10-point-rise error is above.
intermediate_check: Solved intermediates are 27, 51, 204 and 18; none is an option. 240 (24 / 0.10) is not an option.
cheap_bound_check: Liters are continuous, so no whole-number or multiple-of rule applies. No total or denominator bound is readable off the stem, and every option exceeds the 24 liters added. No option strikes.
arith_class_check: No forced class: amounts of liquid need not be whole.
